cases.title: Clicking Add note creates a new note div with textarea
cases.description: Verify that when the user clicks the Add note button (id="add", class="add", data-testid="add-note-button"), a new note is created and appended to the document body as a div element with the class "note" containing a visible, empty textarea (data-testid="note-textarea").

cases.title: Multiple rapid clicks on Add note button create separate notes
cases.description: Verify that the application supports multiple rapid clicks on the Add note button, with each click successfully creating a separate note element containing its own distinct textarea.

cases.title: Real-time Markdown rendering for standard syntax
cases.description: Verify that when the user types standard Markdown syntax such as headers, bold text, italic text, and links into the note textarea (data-testid="note-textarea"), the content is dynamically and correctly rendered in real-time within the main display area (data-testid="note-main"), and changes are immediately reflected in local storage.

cases.title: Handling complex Markdown syntax without errors
cases.description: Verify that the application properly handles complex Markdown syntax without causing crashes or errors, updating both the main display area and local storage immediately as the user types.

cases.title: Graceful fallback for invalid Markdown syntax
cases.description: Verify that when the user inputs invalid Markdown syntax such as unmatched bold markers (**), the application does not crash and displays the raw input when the user exits edit mode by clicking the "Edit" button (data-testid="edit-note-button"), while maintaining local storage updates.

cases.title: Default edit mode upon creating a new note
cases.description: Verify that when a user creates a new note by clicking the add-note-button, the note immediately enters edit mode where the textarea (data-testid="note-textarea") is visible and the main content area (data-testid="note-main") remains hidden.

cases.title: Toggle between edit and view modes using the edit button
cases.description: Verify that clicking the edit-note-button switches the note between edit and view modes. In view mode, note-main is visible and note-textarea is hidden; in edit mode, note-textarea is visible and note-main is hidden.

cases.title: Automatic saving of textarea input to local storage
cases.description: Verify that all changes typed into the note-textarea are automatically saved to local storage, preserving the note's state across sessions.

cases.title: Delete note successfully removes from DOM and localStorage
cases.description: Verify that clicking the delete button (data-testid="delete-note-button") on a note immediately removes the note element from the DOM and removes the corresponding entry from localStorage.

cases.title: Retrieve and display notes from localStorage on page load
cases.description: Verify that when the webpage loads with stored notes in localStorage, the application dynamically creates a div with class 'note' for each entry containing the required tools, edit/delete buttons, main content area, and textarea.

cases.title: Display main div and hide textarea for notes with content on load
cases.description: Verify that for notes retrieved from localStorage that contain content, the content is displayed in the main div (data-testid="note-main") and the textarea (data-testid="note-textarea") is hidden by default.

cases.title: Display textarea and hide main div for notes with no content on load
cases.description: Verify that for notes retrieved from localStorage that have no content, the application shows the textarea (data-testid="note-textarea") and hides the main div (data-testid="note-main") to allow immediate editing.

cases.title: Handle empty localStorage on page load
cases.description: Verify that when the webpage loads and localStorage is empty or returns no notes, no notes are shown on the page.

opinions.feedback: All requirements and test cases are clear, consistent, and fully testable without any blockers.

analysis.analysis: Decomposed the requirements into normal, edge, boundary, and abnormal scenarios based on the provided UI identifiers and specifications for the Notes App: R-1 covers single and rapid multi-click note creation with specific element classes and attributes; R-2 focuses on real-time Markdown rendering, complex syntax handling, graceful fallback for invalid syntax, and local storage updates; R-3 handles the state transitions between view and edit modes and persistence across sessions; R-4 details the DOM and localStorage cleanup upon clicking the delete button; R-5 manages initial page load recovery from localStorage, conditional display of textarea vs main display based on content presence, and handling empty storage states.
